name: Apoptosis — intrinsic (mitochondrial) pathway
summary: Internal stress (DNA damage, growth-factor withdrawal, ER stress) activates BH3-only proteins that overcome BCL-2 and activate BAX/BAK. Mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilisation releases cytochrome c, which builds the apoptosome to activate caspase-9 and then executioner caspase-3.
clinical: Cancer cells often overexpress BCL-2 family survival proteins; venetoclax (BH3 mimetic) restores apoptosis in CLL/AML. p53 loss removes a major route to PUMA/NOXA induction.
outcomes: Apoptosis: DNA fragmentation, blebbing, PS exposure, phagocytic clearance without inflammation

references.label: Singh, Letai & Sarosiek (2019) Nat Rev Mol Cell Biol 20:175 — BCL-2 family

steps.title: 1 · Stress is sensed
steps.text: DNA damage stabilises p53, which induces the BH3-only genes PUMA and NOXA; growth-factor withdrawal releases BIM.

steps.title: 2 · Overcoming BCL-2
steps.text: BH3-only proteins bind anti-apoptotic BCL-2/BCL-xL and directly activate BAX and BAK.

steps.title: 3 · MOMP
steps.text: BAX/BAK oligomerise in the mitochondrial outer membrane, releasing cytochrome c and SMAC. This is usually the point of no return.

steps.title: 4 · Apoptosome
steps.text: Cytochrome c binds APAF-1, which (with dATP) assembles into a heptameric apoptosome that activates caspase-9.

steps.title: 5 · Execution
steps.text: Caspase-9 cleaves and activates caspase-3/7. SMAC neutralises XIAP so caspases are not blocked. Caspase-3 cleaves hundreds of substrates, dismantling the cell.
